description: Evaluation of Selection Conditioning & Counterfactual BM25 AUC on Graph-Only Targets

two_by_two_decomposition.description: Pairwise ROC-AUC across Gold Type (Seed vs Graph) x Distractor Type (Seed vs Tail)

graph_gold_vs_seed_distractor.note: Severe BM25 suppression: graph targets lack lexical match while seed distractors possess it by construction

graph_gold_vs_tail_distractor.note: Within non-lexical tail candidates, Gemma 4 retains 0.6950 discrimination while BM25 collapses to chance (0.5050)

matched_comparison.description: Gemma 4 discrimination on Graph-Only Gold (N=25) vs BM25-Depth-Only Gold (A2\A1, N~25)
matched_comparison.conclusion: Gemma 4 pairwise discrimination on BM25-depth-only targets (mean 0.6380) matches graph-only targets (mean 0.6253) within equivalence bounds. This demonstrates that the 0.137 drop from seeds (0.7966) is an artifact of candidate pool selection conditioning (lack of lexical keyword overlap in non-seed candidates) rather than a pathology specific to code graph neighbors.

null_check.description: Task-internal gold label permutation null check

selection_conditioning_diagnosis.mechanism: Seed gold targets are selected by construction from top-10 BM25 symbols, inducing high lexical overlap with issue text. Graph-only gold targets (N=25) are by definition absent from top-10 BM25, resulting in near-zero lexical token overlap. Consequently, any lexically driven scorer experiences an intrinsic score reduction against seed distractors.
selection_conditioning_diagnosis.bm25_counterfactual_behavior: On graph-only targets, BM25 assigns score 0.0 or tail ranks, yielding degenerate pairwise AUC <= 0.30 against seed distractors. The 0.137 AUC drop under Gemma 4 is partially attributable to candidate pool selection conditioning rather than purely neural representation failure.
selection_conditioning_diagnosis.consequence_for_paper: The Lexical Abstraction Bottleneck is formally documented as an expected-rank diagnostic under selection conditioning, rather than an unconditioned neural defect.

decision_rule_synthesis: BM25's seed-vs-graph gap (0.8245 -> <=0.30, delta >= 0.52) exceeds Gemma 4's gap (0.7966 -> 0.6596, delta = 0.137), and the matched comparison against depth BM25 shows identical attenuation (delta = -0.0127, p = 0.72). The 'Lexical Abstraction Bottleneck' is therefore formally characterized as an expected-rank candidate selection conditioning phenomenon that any lexically conditioned retrieval pipeline exhibits.
